text.p: The Strober Organization Inc said on Wednesday it had received an unsolicited proposal to be acquired for $6.50 per share, in cash.
The bid tops a bid of $6 a share the company agreed to with Hamilton Acquisition LLC on November 11, 1996.
Strober did not identify the source of the $6.50 a share offer that values the company at $35 million on a fully diluted basis.
This third party proposal is subject to a financing contingency, receipt of certain governmental approvals and other customary conditions, Strober said.
Strober said the third party is also prepared to assume the termination fee and related costs and expenses arising from Strober's definitive merger agreement with Hamilton Acquisition LLC.
Strober said there can be no assurance that it will reach a definitive agreement with the third party, which proposes completing the deal in January 1997.
Strober's principal stockholders owning approximately 62 percent of its outstanding common stock had entered into a proxy agreement agreeing to vote their shares in favor of the Hamilton merger.
However, termination of the Hamilton merger agreement by the company would terminate the proxy power in the agreement, Strober said.
